interference fringes of the same inclination are a major source of error when measuring the reflection coefficient of plane parallel plate beamsplitters.

the coefficient of reflection of a plane parallel plate beam splitter is not twice as much as that of a single plate, but depends on the angle of incidence of the light beam and the thickness of the plate, with an average value of about 1.5 times the single plate value.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for a plane parallel plate beam splitter, the coefficient of reflection should be taken as twice that for a single reflection, only if the incident angle is small, and if the lateral displacement of reflected beams is small, or if the beams are integrated by an appropriate optical element.
for a plane parallel plate beam splitter the reflection coefficient is not twice but about 1.3 times that of a single reflection, if the beam splitter follows an integrating sphere or similar device.

for a plane parallel plate beam splitter the coefficient of reflection is not equal to twice the reflection coefficient of a single surface, but is a complicated function of the angle of incidence and of the thickness of the beam splitter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coefficient of reflection of a plane parallel plate beam splitter is not a constant value but depends on the angle of incidence.
the coefficient of reflection of a plane parallel plate beam splitter is not equal to twice that of the reflection of a single surface.
the average coefficient of reflection of beam splitters is always less than twice that of the single surface reflection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coefficient of reflection of a beam splitter should be determined experimentally.
one should be very careful in interpreting the results of measurements of reflection of laser beams by plane parallel plates.
, for most practical purposes, the coefficient of reflection of a plane parallel plate is equal to the coefficient of reflection from one of its surfaces.
